text:
laura: Quick question—newly married engineer updated beneficiaries off-platform and wants that reflected for their 401k and HSA. HR recorded spouse but the plan vendor shows old beneficiary. What steps to reconcile and do we need a new signed beneficiary form?

elaine: If the vendor has the old beneficiary on file we need a vendor-signed acceptance of the new beneficiary form. Employee should complete the vendor's beneficiary form (many have their own doc) and sign. We also accept a notarized or e-signed vendor form if vendor allows.

mike: For 401k specifically, update needs to be done with the plan trustee. Employee should submit the trustee beneficiary form. Until vendor confirms, payroll should not change plan records.

laura: Do we need manager or People Ops approval for the change?

elaine: No approval needed unless change is to a trust or a third-party. Just ensure form is complete and signed. Capture date of marriage certificate only if vendor requests proof — usually not required for simple spouse designation.

payroll: Also note: if employee has QDRO or any divorce flag previously, vendor may require clearance. Payroll will hold final distribution flags until vendor confirms beneficiary update.

laura: What about HSA beneficiary — can it be updated the same way?

mike: HSA beneficiary usually has a separate form with the HSA custodian. Employee submits HSA beneficiary form to HSA provider. Keep copies in HR file and note the custodian confirmation email.

elaine: Checklist I'll add to the offboarding/benefits change packet: 1) Signed vendor trustee beneficiary form for 401k; 2) HSA custodian beneficiary form; 3) Vendor confirmation email (acceptance) for each; 4) If legacy QDRO or locked accounts exist, vendor clearance required.
